messages: maria: Quick check — the pool dropdown now shows an autoscale badge + an SLO mini-preview. UX question: should the SLO preview be visible for pools that are capacity-locked (min==max)? zack: I think hide it when locked. Preview implies the pool can change to meet SLOs, which is misleading. aj: +1 but also think it's useful for comparison. Compromise: show a greyed/annotated preview with a tooltip: 'SLO preview unavailable when autoscaling is disabled'. priya: Engineering note: we can flag pool.canSimulate. If false, return a snapshot string instead of a simulated curve. That string could be: 'snapshot: p95 220ms @ est +$0.12/hr'. sam: Accessibility: tooltip must be keyboard-focusable. Any small graph in the dropdown needs alt text or a textual fallback like 'p95 X ms, cost Y/hr'. oliver: Copy nit: prefer 'SLO preview (estimate)' as label so users know it's not exact. Avoid words like 'guarantee'. maria: Also suggestion: sort dropdown to surface 'Recommended' pools first (based on simScore), show a small badge 'Recommended for SLO' — but if the recommended pool is locked, show an inline caution: 'Capacity locked — may not meet SLO unless you enable autoscaling or raise min.' aj: When user selects a recommended+locked pool, show an inline micro-confirm in the selector: 'Proceed? This pool is locked at N GPUs and may not hit target.' Buttons: 'Use anyway' / 'Choose another'. Keep it inline, no modal. priya: Impl detail: API will return metadata: supportsBurst, isLocked, canSimulate, simScoreText. Frontend renders simScoreText when canSimulate==false. sam: ARIA snippet for the dropdown header suggestion: ``` SLO preview shows estimated p95 latency and cost; previews may be disabled for capacity-locked pools ``` design-bot: Preview: https://preview.redwood.design/branch/pool-dropdown-slo — includes greyed preview state, recommended sorting, and keyboard walkthrough. maria: OK action items: AJ finalizes copy + microcopy strings, Priya to add simScoreText to pool API, Sam to add keyboard/alt-text tests, Oliver to review recommended sorting logic. I'll update the Figma frame and acceptance criteria.
